column1: # 8 nodes x 8 GPUs. Default flavor k3_64x{mem}: K3's 93 layers (full attention on every fourth and the last),
# MN_FLAVOR picks another flavor ({mem}: 80g or 141g by hardware); MN_SEQ pins the row's length over MN_SEQ_FORCE.
# +core marks the rows only 8 nodes answer (k8s.sh apply 8 +core runs just those, about 50 minutes).
# Every row keeps 524288 tokens per step and data parallelism 2 (or 1); the extra GPUs go to PP across nodes and
# to a bigger model, while TP, CP and EP stay inside a node unless the row says otherwise.
# The 11-08 model on four times the GPUs: PP 8 (29 layers allow at most 2 virtual stages per rank).
# The 93-layer model: PP across the eight nodes; 4 virtual stages per rank is K3's 32-stage pipeline.
# The same cell again right after: its difference is the noise floor of every pair.
# Four times the experts instead: EP 8 inside a node against EP 16 across two nodes.
# Long context: CP 8 x TP 4 spans four nodes, no PP, two sequences of 128K per step.
# The main layout compiled (local regions and flex autotuning; the cache stays on the shared volume).
